_what: DISCLOSED USEFUL LIVES, read from each company's OWN audited accounting-policies note. [R-TERM-01] requires the terminal's maintenance charge to rest on a DISCLOSED life and REFUSES one this desk chose (SIGCM clause 1), so the life has to be sourced before a terminal can be rebuilt — and until it is, the census can only say 'not sourced'. This file is where that research accumulates, one name at a time, so the next rebuild reads it instead of re-opening the filing.
_how: Every entry names the FILE, the NOTE and the ROUTE the figure came by (text layer or OCR off the rendered pixels), on the same footing as the four-field rule. A RANGE IS RECORDED AS A RANGE: most policy notes give a band per asset class and not a single number, and collapsing that to one figure here would be this desk choosing the life under cover of a citation. The weighted life a terminal actually needs is derived at rebuild from the property, plant and equipment note's own composition, which is a further sourcing step and is NOT done here.
_binds: Nothing reads this yet except the census's 'disclosed' column. A rebuild that uses one of these lives commits it to its own terminal_record, which is what the gate and the census then read [R-ENF-01].

ADNOCLS.source: ADNOC L&S plc, consolidated financial statements FY2025 (PwC-audited, signed 10 February 2026), accounting policies. ALREADY REGISTERED BY THAT STUDY as the input life_tankers with the full policy sentence; recorded here so every sourced life sits in one place.
ADNOCLS.route: already committed as a four-field input in the study's own register
ADNOCLS.against_the_terminal: this study's terminal implies 50.0 years (1/g at g=2.0%) against a 25-year tanker life, so it UNDER-charges by 2x on the headline class — and its invested-capital base is NET BOOK ppe plus working capital plus goodwill, which is not a replacement-cost base at all, so the life is the second thing to fix there rather than the first.

dry_docking_life.source: the same accounting-policies note, under 'Dry docking': "Major dry docking is capitalised when incurred and is depreciated over the period until the next major dry dock which is normally 60 months." The class table gives only the 2-5 year band; this sentence gives the figure, and the earlier reading took the band and stopped.
dry_docking_life.route: text layer, FY2025 accounting policies, confirmed identical in FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024

ADNOCLS.why_the_terminal_refused: MEASURED 04-Sep-2026, and it sharpens the earlier stop rather than repeating it. The rebuild computed maintenance as the WHOLE gross base at 25 years — 303,803 against book property depreciation of 385,487, i.e. 78.8% of it — so terminal free cash flow exceeded terminal profit and the module refused. THE 25-YEAR LIFE IS DISCLOSED FOR TANKERS, NOT FOR THE BASE. Applying one class's life to every class is the life-this-desk-chose error wearing a citation, and it is what produced the refusal.
ADNOCLS.what_the_disclosure_does_support: The gross cost IS disclosed by class and every class has its own disclosed life, so only the vessel line mixes two — hulls at 25 years and dry-docking components at 5 — and only that line is unsplit. The other four classes are 315,131 of 7,595,070 (4.1%), and their depreciation is bounded by their own disclosed ranges to between 23,993 (longest lives) and 61,785 (shortest). Subtracting from the 385,487 the company reports across notes 5 and 6 leaves the vessel line depreciating 323,702 to 361,494, and solving (V-x)/25 + x/5 for that BOUNDS THE DRY-DOCKING COMPONENT TO 2.79%-6.04% OF THE VESSEL LINE. That is arithmetic on the disclosure, not a choice.
ADNOCLS.the_next_step_is_named: Maintenance at the disclosed lives on the GROSS base equals book depreciation on that base by construction, straight-line — which is why the honest charge is near 385,487 rather than 303,803, and why the refusal reverses at any point inside the bound above. WHAT IS STILL NOT SOURCED is the step from historical cost to CURRENT cost, which [R-TERM-01] requires and which a ship market can actually supply: broker-quoted secondhand and newbuild prices are an OBSERVED price for a vessel in a way they are not for a kiln ([R-LENS-03] says so). That is the input to find, and until it is found the charge would rest on replacement cost equalling historical cost, which for a fleet of this age is an assumption and not a reading. DO NOT REBUILD THIS TERMINAL ON THE NAIVE 25-YEAR CHARGE — that is what refused, and it refused correctly.
ADNOCLS.exemplar_note: This is the model report [R-ENF-01 EXTENDED 04-Sep], so its terminal is inherited by every study built by opening it. Its terminal currently sits 7.5% BELOW its own NOPAT floor, and the correction indicated above RAISES it — which is stated here because L-289 forbids reading the direction off the census, and because a correction moving an exemplar's value up is exactly the kind nobody chases.

weighted_life_derived.identity: depreciable cost / the year's depreciation charge
weighted_life_derived.source: Fertiglobe plc, 2025 Annual Report, note 7 property, plant and equipment — the cost and accumulated-depreciation table at 31 December 2025, and the 'Depreciation and impairment' movement row for the year.
weighted_life_derived.why_derived_and_not_chosen: THE DISCLOSED BANDS CANNOT BE COLLAPSED WITHOUT CHOOSING. Buildings 10-50, plant and equipment 5-30, fixtures 3-10: any single figure taken from those is this desk picking a life, which [R-TERM-01] refuses outright. What the note ALSO discloses is the composition at COST and the year's charge, and their ratio is an IDENTITY rather than an assumption — the composite life the company's own accounts are actually running. It is LABELLED derived, on the same footing as capex derived by dPPE + D&A and EGCH's years derived from disclosed rates.
weighted_life_derived.the_impairment_caveat_and_why_it_does_no: The movement row is labelled 'Depreciation and impairment', so in a year carrying an impairment the ratio would understate the life. This report states at note 12 that 'no impairments were required for the year ended 31 December 2025', so the row is pure depreciation and the identity is exact. IN A YEAR WITH AN IMPAIRMENT THIS DERIVATION WOULD NOT BE AVAILABLE, and that is a property of the disclosure rather than of the method.
weighted_life_derived.coherence_check: The derived 22.04 years sits INSIDE the disclosed plant-and-equipment band of 5-30, and plant and equipment is 94.6% of the depreciable cost base — so the figure the arithmetic produces and the class that dominates the base agree. That is the check that makes a derived life usable rather than merely arithmetic.
weighted_life_derived.against_the_retired_terminal: The retired terminal charges g x IC, so it implies a replacement cycle of 1/g = 50.0 years at this study's 2% terminal — 2.27 TIMES the life this company's own accounts depreciate its assets over. That is the [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO] direction reversal measured on one name with its own numbers: in a pegged market the identity does not starve the asset base, it flatters it, and correcting it moves the value DOWN.

EGCH.source: Egyptian Chemical Industries (KIMA), annual financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2025, notes to the financial statements, note 1-5 'الأصول الثابتة وإهلاكاتها' (fixed assets and their depreciation), sub-heading 'الإهلاك' (depreciation), page 31: 'يتم تحميل الإهلاك على قائمة الدخل وفقا لطريقة القسط الثابت وفقا لمعدلات تتماشي مع العمر الإنتاجي المقدر لكل أصل عدا الأراضي' — depreciation is charged on a straight-line basis at rates matching each asset's estimated useful life, land excepted — followed by a table of DEPRECIATION RATES per asset type.
EGCH.route: OCR OFF THE RENDERED PIXELS, then READ AS AN IMAGE. The filing carries NO text layer (48 bytes extracted across 48 pages), so pdftotext returns nothing. Tesseract at 200dpi and again at 450dpi located the note and read the asset-class names cleanly, and could NOT read the Arabic-Indic digits reliably at either resolution — one pass rendered 9.5 as '5 ث9' and 4.75 as 'د" ؛/'. A RATES TABLE HAS NO INTERNAL ARITHMETIC TO FOOT AGAINST, so the usual arbiter is unavailable and the extractor's confidence is worth nothing on its own. The figures below were read from the rendered page as an image at 450dpi, which is the route recorded.
EGCH.years_are_derived_not_disclosed: THE COMPANY DISCLOSES RATES; THE YEARS BESIDE THEM ARE 100/rate AND ARE LABELLED DERIVED. An identity is not an assumption, and the label is what keeps the two apart — the same discipline [R-FCAL-01 AMENDED] applies to capex derived by ΔPPE + D&A.
EGCH.cells_not_read: Three cells in the buildings row are NOT recorded because their digits could not be read with confidence even from the rendered page: an entry for the cinema and cafeteria building, one for iron and steel buildings that appears to be a range, and the furniture and fittings row, which falls on a page boundary in the crop. They are named here rather than guessed — a figure this desk cannot read is a figure this desk does not use (SIGCM clause 8), and none of the three is a production asset the terminal turns on.
EGCH.not_yet_collapsed: A RANGE IS RECORDED AS A RANGE and here it is very wide — 5 to 50 years — because the table mixes a residential building at 2% with passenger cars at 20%. The weighted life a terminal needs comes from this company's own property, plant and equipment composition; on a fertiliser producer the classes that carry the value are the plants at 6% (buildings) and 3.95% to 9.5% (machinery), i.e. roughly 10 to 25 years, and establishing that weighting is a further sourcing step not done here.

AIRARABIA.source: Air Arabia PJSC and its subsidiaries, consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025, note 4 material accounting policies, property and equipment: 'The useful lives are applied, as follows'. Land granted by the Government of Sharjah is not depreciated, 'as it is deemed to have an infinite life'. Residual values and the 2024 reassessment are from note 5, property and equipment.
AIRARABIA.cross_check: THE TABLE PRINTS ITS OWN COMPARATIVE COLUMN — 2025 beside 2024 — and every class is identical in both, which is the cross-check inside one document. The FY2024 statements committed beside it carry no text layer (65 bytes) and were not needed.
AIRARABIA.an_apparent_contradiction_resolved: The FY2025 policy note opens 'During the year, the Group changed the estimated useful life applied to certain assets ... refer Note 5', while the table it introduces shows NO change between 2025 and 2024. Note 5 settles it: the reassessment was 'during the year ended 31 December 2024', effective 1 October 2024 — aircraft lives raised from 15 to 20 years, residual values cut from 20% to 7-8% of original cost, quantified at AED 29.3mn on net assets and AED 26.7mn on net profit. THE OPENING SENTENCE IS PRIOR-YEAR PROSE CARRIED FORWARD IN THE COMPANY'S OWN FILING. It is recorded because a reader who stopped at that sentence would date a change to the wrong year, and because a disclosure that contradicts its own table is the shape this house is supposed to notice — it is theirs and not ours, and the resolution is theirs too.
AIRARABIA.why_this_name_matters_here: AIRARABIA is one of the seven terminals charging LESS than their own book depreciation and one of the three doing it while sitting more than 10% BELOW the price. Its retired terminal implies a replacement cycle of 1/g = 40 years against a DISCLOSED aircraft life of 20 — it charges roughly half the maintenance the disclosure implies, on the asset class that carries essentially all the value. Correcting it moves the value DOWN and therefore AWAY from the price, which is [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO]'s point and the side of the correction this house has never measured.
AIRARABIA.not_yet_collapsed: A RANGE IS RECORDED AS A RANGE, though this one is unusually well determined: an airline's value sits in aircraft and engines, both disclosed at a single 20 years rather than a band. The weighting is still a further sourcing step, and the 7-8% residual belongs in it — maintenance at replacement cost over 20 years against a 7-8% residual is not the same charge as over 15 against 20%.
